solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Comedian's outside broadcast hard work, live screening

definitions.note: possessive 's is read as 'is', so the comedian is the answer

indicators.note: to screen something is to hide it behind a cover, so the word for live wraps round the rest

parts.note: to live is to be, giving BE
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A comic's TV special is filmed on location: a hard day's work shown live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comedian's' reads as 'Comedian is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the British-born American entertainer famed for wisecracks and wartime troop shows was a celebrated comedian.

clue.text: Brown is right in the firing line

indicators.note: the letter for right goes in the line word

parts.note: the OCHE is the line darts players throw from

explanation.surface: A political figure called Brown is right in the firing line of critics.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCHE is the line behind which a darts player stands to throw, a British pub-game term.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an earthy yellowish-brown pigment, so a shade of brown.

clue.text: This foreman may be asked to store gold for auditor?

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the pieces are taken by how they would be heard

parts.note: to store is to HOUSE, and AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A works foreman is asked to keep gold safe for an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but means a listener; 'foreman' is the foreman of a jury, not a factory boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal formula: the traditional question the court clerk puts to the jury's spokesperson asking for the verdict.

clue.text: Character at Savoy I'm surprised to see in lead? That is a surprise!

indicators.note: the exclamation is set in the chemical symbol for lead

parts.note: PB is the chemical symbol for lead
OOH is an exclamation of surprise
AH is another cry of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to find a Savoy performer leading, and saying so.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy is the London theatre of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the pompous Lord High Everything Else in The Mikado is a character in a Savoy opera.

clue.text: City Road, near which one's pulled into greasy spoon

indicators.note: a vehicle pulls into a roadside café, so these letters are drawn inside the café word

parts.note: a greasy spoon is a cheap café, informally a CAFF in Britain
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A city street with a cheap roadside café where a driver stops.
explanation.walkthrough: A CAFF is British slang for a basic café serving fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Welsh capital is a city on the Severn estuary.

clue.text: With a will not one African

parts.note: SHANT, shan't, is a contraction meaning shall not, will not
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An African who refuses to make a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of a people of Ghana is African.

clue.text: Cryptically take a little sum out of a bank account?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to remove a bit, the prefix de- meaning take away

definitions.text: sum out of a bank account?
definitions.meaning: an amount withdrawn or charged against an account

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter invites taking a small sum from a bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: The word split as DE + BIT means take a bit away.
explanation.definitionFit: Banking: an entry recording money taken from an account, the opposite of a credit.

clue.text: What comes after me with New England accessory?

parts.note: in the sol-fa scale me (mi) is followed by FA

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of the country are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a fashion accessory from New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal, not part of New England; it rearranges ENGLAND to NDANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a gaudy ornament or trinket worn for show, a fancy accessory.

clue.text: "Effort to pull not at all cunning" — the essence of Anthony Eden

parts.note: a HEAVE is a great effort to pull
NONE means not at all, as in none the wiser
ART is cunning, craftiness

indicators.note: the essence is the core, the middle letter of the name

explanation.surface: A political sketch: the essence of Prime Minister Anthony Eden was effort without guile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eden' looks like part of the statesman's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical sense: the Garden of Eden is a paradise, perfect bliss in this world.

clue.text: Great rockers on stage introducing woman forbidding everything!

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another sits just before it

parts.note: a famous British rock band of the 1960s onwards

indicators.note: the stage word takes in the following pieces, introducing them into its middle

parts.note: a stage of a journey is a LEG
SHE is the pronoun for a woman
to forbid is to BAN

explanation.surface: A legendary rock band takes the stage and a woman bans the whole lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Who are a famous British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the entire lot or affair, everything included.

clue.text: Smear campaign initially BBC denied, due a wrangle

indicators.note: to wrangle is to argue and tangle, so the letters are jumbled
the broadcaster's letters are denied one, which is removed
initially points to the first letter of campaign

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smear campaign that the BBC refused to air, leading to a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C from 'campaign'; 'denied' removes it from BBC, leaving BB, which 'wrangle' mixes with DUE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to daub over is to smear or plaster with a sticky substance.

clue.text: Blind drunk in event one's opening?

indicators.note: the single article prises the jumbled letters open and sits inside them
drunk means reeling and mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
one is A, the indefinite article; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone blind drunk at a party where one is opening proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' looks like part of 'blind drunk' but is the definition; the A goes between the last two letters of the rearranged fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Compound sense: a window shade of horizontal slats is called a Venetian blind, so the word alone stands for it.

clue.text: No way in hell that's funny — it's repellent comedy

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so these letters are taken in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
UGH is the exclamation at something repellent

explanation.surface: An indignant viewer insists a dreadful comedy show is anything but funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' is the anagram signal on NO WAY IN HELL. The answer is the title of a 1970s British sitcom set in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the title of a British television sitcom from the late 1970s, so a comedy.

clue.text: Artless states of North America with which I'm associated?

parts.note: things with which I'm associated are those to which I've ties, read as I'VE TIES

explanation.surface: A patriot asks whether his native American states are rather artless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like a political word but means conditions; I'VE TIES is the speaker's link to those states.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: simple, unworldly conditions or acts are innocent naivety, artlessness.

clue.text: See 13
Notice son of Paris swelling ego up, being miserable

parts.note: an AD, advertisement, is a notice

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, backwards
the French son swells the ego from within, inside it

parts.note: FILS is French for son

explanation.surface: A French son with an inflated ego is having a wretched time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole container EFILSGO, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a wretched, unhappy existence, a life fit only for a hound.

clue.text: Quiet old inn (not yet closed) girl somehow means to preserve

indicators.note: somehow means by some unexplained means, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a word not yet closed lacks its final letter

explanation.surface: A quiet old pub, still open, and a girl looking for some way to keep things fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket sits after 'inn', but it is the girl who is cut short: the letters only work with GIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: the super-cold liquefied gas is used to freeze and so preserve biological samples.

clue.text: By force, make GP continue suppressing onset of asthma

indicators.note: the doctor and the continuing hold the asthma letter down between them, kept inside

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, DR
to continue is to GO ON

indicators.note: the onset is the first letter

explanation.surface: Forcing a family doctor to keep treating an asthma attack.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a British family doctor; 'make' belongs to the definition, giving the verb sense of compel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dragoon is to coerce, compel someone by force.

clue.text: See 17
I left force, subdued by aforementioned individuals

indicators.note: in a down clue the subdued pieces lie beneath the word that holds them down

parts.note: THESE refers back to individuals already mentioned
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Someone who left the police force, kept down by the people mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the definition: the ego or one's own identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Philosophical sense: the ego, one's own person, as referred to by the first-person pronoun.

clue.text: Dorsally, Maeve's heart contains almost completely empty vessel

indicators.note: dorsal means towards the back, so the assembled letters are read back to front
the heart letters hold the next piece inside them
the heart of the name is its middle letters
almost completely means all but the last letter

parts.note: empty means VACANT

explanation.surface: An anatomy note: Maeve's heart contains a nearly empty blood vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dorsally' (towards the back) turns round the whole assembly AVACANEV, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the great vein returning blood to the heart is a major blood vessel.

clue.text: A sucker, I enrolled for a doctorate?

indicators.note: enrolling for a course puts one inside it

parts.note: a PhD is a doctorate, giving A PHD

explanation.surface: Someone admits being a sucker for signing up to a doctorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' means a sap-sucking insect, not a gullible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the greenfly feeds by sucking plant sap, so it is a sucker.

clue.text: Fake tigers at zoo limits

indicators.note: the answer lies within the limits of these words, hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Imitation tigers on show within the zoo's boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' says the answer is held within 'tigers at zoo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something substitute or imitation is fake, an inferior replacement.

clue.text: Topic 20?

definitions.meaning: the answer to 20 down is a phrase whose second word also means the objective first-person pronoun, so 'the' plus that pronoun

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking what topic another clue suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the second word of 20 down for its equivalent pronoun, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the subject or main idea of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Mah-jonggathon for drunken stopouts?

parts.note: mah-jongg is played with tiles, so an all-night session is literally an evening spent on the tiles; the idiom means a night of drinking out

explanation.surface: An all-night tile game marathon for revellers who stay out drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means a night out on the town; mah-jongg players literally sit over tiles all night.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a riotous evening out drinking, as cats were once said to roam the roofs.

clue.text: Emphatically, compiler does not like a set in line

definitions.meaning: the setter saying '...', an emphatic refusal, when run together
describing teeth all of one size and form, a set lined up evenly

explanation.surface: A crossword setter firmly refuses to like a neatly lined-up set.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as I SO DON'T, the setter speaking emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoological term: having all teeth alike in shape and size, like a uniform set in a row.

clue.text: Something that eases section off with increased regularity

indicators.note: with the section letter taken off, it is removed from the start

parts.note: a SOFTENER is something that eases or softens

explanation.surface: A product to ease a section of the body, taken more and more often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes S from SOFTENER.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word meaning frequently, so more frequently, a rarer form of 'more often'.
